questions.question: What is the main production responsibility split between an OpenAI model and the application?
options: The model owns authorization while the application owns wording.
The model proposes outputs or tool calls; the application owns trust boundaries, validation, authorization, and side effects.
The platform automatically validates every business invariant.
The browser should call OpenAI directly so the backend cannot change results.
questions.explanation: A model can generate content and propose actions, but trusted application code must enforce identity, permissions, semantic rules, and execution policy.

questions.question: How should a team choose a lower-cost model for ticket extraction?
options: Pick the model with the shortest name.
Start with the cheapest model and skip quality measurement.
Establish a representative quality floor with a capable model, then verify that the smaller model preserves it within latency and cost targets.
Use a reasoning model for every request.
questions.explanation: Model selection is evidence-based. Quality must meet the product floor before cost and latency optimization is accepted.

questions.question: When is a strict structured response more appropriate than a function tool?
options: When the model should return typed data for the application to render, without requesting an external action.
When the model should issue a refund immediately.
When the application has no schema.
When authorization should be delegated to the model.
questions.explanation: Structured responses define returned data shape. Function tools are for requesting access to application data or actions and require a separate execution boundary.

questions.question: Why should a refund tool omit an account ID that the authenticated session already knows?
options: It makes the JSON larger.
It prevents the model from choosing a different account and keeps resource identity in trusted state.
It guarantees the refund is always correct.
It disables retries.
questions.explanation: Trusted identity should come from the authenticated application context, not from model-generated arguments that can be manipulated.

questions.question: What is the main trade-off when file search returns fewer chunks?
options: It can reduce token use and latency but may miss evidence needed for answer quality.
It always increases retrieval recall.
It removes the need for source eligibility filters.
It automatically pins the model snapshot.
questions.explanation: A smaller evidence set is cheaper and faster, but retrieval recall can fall. Measure retrieval and answer quality separately.

questions.question: Why can streaming be unsuitable for a high-risk output path?
options: Streaming always costs more per token.
Partial output may reach the user before whole-output moderation or validation completes.
Streaming cannot carry text.
Streaming disables request IDs.
questions.explanation: Streaming improves perceived latency, but partial completions are harder to evaluate before display. High-risk flows may need buffering or human review.

questions.question: A rate-limited request fails. What retry policy protects shared capacity?
options: Retry immediately in an infinite loop.
Retry every request at the same fixed instant.
Use capped exponential backoff with jitter, respect the deadline, and shed optional work when pressure persists.
Increase every request's output budget.
questions.explanation: Backoff and jitter reduce synchronized retry pressure. Attempts must remain bounded because unsuccessful requests also consume limit budget.

questions.question: A tool timed out after a side effect may have completed. What must happen before retrying?
options: Ask the model to guess whether it completed.
Change the tool name and submit again.
Look up the stable idempotency key and return the recorded result or safely resume the same operation.
Disable observability.
questions.explanation: A timeout is ambiguous. Idempotency lets the executor determine whether the operation already happened without duplicating it.

questions.question: Which evidence is sufficient to promote a model or API migration?
options: A lower average latency alone.
One successful manual prompt.
Passing task, safety, contract, load, observability, canary, and rollback gates defined for the product risk.
A provider changelog entry.
questions.explanation: Migration changes can affect behavior, schemas, failure modes, and operations. Promotion needs a complete, product-specific evidence set and a tested rollback.
